answer: Sybil resistance relies on dynamic graph topology: reputation enforces an exponential temporal half-life requiring sustained validation cycles rather than sudden attempts to forge synthetic trust. As transactional streams ingest across our network wharf, malicious clusters remain isolated. Freshly spawned identities, lacking inbound transitivity, sit at the base of the trust knoll with near-zero eigenvector centrality, strictly barring them from achieving consensus thresholds.
